brief: Inventors and firsts from South Africa

shortlist.fact: South African entrepreneur Mark Shuttleworth, the first African in space, took a radio call from Nelson Mandela and a 14-year-old girl who asked him to marry her.
shortlist.why: I knew he went to space but nobody ever told me Mandela phoned him and some teenager proposed to him from Earth in the same conversation — that's the bit I'm sending.
shortlist.title: Mark Shuttleworth

candidate.fact: South African entrepreneur Mark Shuttleworth, the first African in space, took a radio call from Nelson Mandela and a 14-year-old girl who asked him to marry her.
candidate.passage:
From space, he spoke via video link to Thabo Mbeki, then president of South Africa, as part of the Freedom Day celebrations marking the end of apartheid.
He also had a radio conversation with Nelson Mandela and a 14-year-old South African girl, Michelle Foster, who asked him to marry her.
candidate.reasoning: The marriage proposal from a terminally ill 14-year-old during a Mandela radio call is a detail almost nobody knows.

shortlist.fact: Cardiac surgeon Christiaan Barnard said of his lab assistant Hamilton Naki: "technically, he is a better surgeon than I am."
shortlist.why: A world-famous surgeon saying his Black lab assistant was better than him is a wild flex that flips everything you'd assume about who gets credit in that story.
shortlist.title: Hamilton Naki

candidate.fact: Cardiac surgeon Christiaan Barnard said of his lab assistant Hamilton Naki: "technically, he is a better surgeon than I am."
candidate.passage: Barnard: "A liver transplant is much more difficult than a heart transplant… [doctors who work with Naki] tell me that Hamilton can do all the various aspects of liver transplantation, which I can't do. So technically, he is a better surgeon than I am."
candidate.reasoning: The world's first heart transplant surgeon admitting an untrained black technician was technically better is a striking, quotable reversal.

shortlist.fact: Sasol's Secunda plant is the world's largest single point source of greenhouse gas, emitting 56.5 Mt of CO2 a year — more than the entire country of Portugal.
shortlist.why: I knew Sasol was big but I never knew one plant here out-pollutes an entire European country — that's the kind of thing that makes the group chat go quiet.

candidate.fact: Sasol's Secunda plant is the world's largest single point source of greenhouse gas, emitting 56.5 Mt of CO2 a year — more than the entire country of Portugal.
candidate.passage: Sasol's Secunda CTL plant is, as of 2020, the world's largest point source of greenhouse gas, at 56.5 Mt/a CO2, a status which persists during the 2020s, with the complex producing more carbon dioxide than the country of Portugal at the close of 2023.
candidate.reasoning: Most South Africans know Sasol as a fuel company but not that a single Secunda plant out-emits an entire European country.

shortlist.fact: Penny Heyns is the only woman in Olympic history to win both the 100 m and 200 m breaststroke, at Atlanta in 1996 — South Africa's first post-apartheid Olympic gold medallist.
shortlist.why: I knew she won gold but I had no idea it was a record no other woman has ever matched, and the post-apartheid first makes it hit harder.
shortlist.title: Penelope Heyns

candidate.fact: Penny Heyns is the only woman in Olympic history to win both the 100 m and 200 m breaststroke, at Atlanta in 1996 — South Africa's first post-apartheid Olympic gold medallist.
candidate.passage: Penelope ("Penny") Heyns OIS (born 8 November 1974) is a South African former swimmer, who is best known for being the only woman in the history of the Olympic Games to have won both the 100 m and 200 m breaststroke events – at the 1996 Atlanta Olympic Games – making her South Africa's first post-apartheid Olympic gold medallist following South Africa's re-admission to the Games in 1992.
candidate.reasoning: Most South Africans know Heyns won gold in 1996, but not that she is the only woman ever to take both breaststroke titles, nor that she was the country's first post-apartheid champion.
